SI-4_title.answer: Multivariate brain-cognition associations in euthymic bipolar disorder

NM2-1_modeling_methods.detail: The study developed normative models of cortical thickness using a generalized additive model (GAM). They harmonized data by regressing age, sex and scanning protocol (site as a random effect) on cortical thickness using GAM implemented in R package mgcv.
NM2-1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We harmonised the normative-HC data, including the 26 HCs recruited to BLISS, for each ROI by regressing age, sex and scanning protocol (i.e., site; as a random effect) on cortical thickness using a generalised additive model. The correction was performed in R using the package mgcv
NM2-1_modeling_methods.location: Little2024.pdf.md: Section 2.4.2 Normative model of cortical thickness

NM2-2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness measures were obtained for 68 anatomical regions of interest (ROIs) using the Desikan-Killiany atlas from FreeSurfer processing of T1-weighted MRI scans.
NM2-2_response_variable.supporting_text: cortical thickness measures were obtained for 68 anatomical regions of interest (ROIs) for each participant using the Desikan-Killiany atlas

NM2-3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model used age and sex as fixed effects and scanning protocol/site as a random effect to model cortical thickness. These covariates were regressed out to harmonize the data across sites.
NM2-3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: regressing age, sex and scanning protocol (i.e., site; as a random effect) on cortical thickness using a generalised additive model
